CVX.rationale: Chevron's Q1 2026 results reveal a company with strong operational execution but significant near-term earnings headwinds. Production surged 15% YoY to 3,858 MBOED driven by Hess integration, and adjusted EPS of $1.41 beat consensus of $0.97 by 45%. However, reported EPS of $1.11 was down 44.5% YoY, dragged by ~$2.9B in unfavorable timing effects (LIFO and derivative marks) and a $360M legal reserve charge. Operating cash flow collapsed to $2.51B from $5.19B YoY due to $4.9B working capital headwind from sharp commodity price increases. The balance sheet remains solid with $189B equity and a 0.6 beta, but ROCE deteriorated to 4.5% (reported) from 8.3% a year ago. Valuation is stretched: P/E of 32.2 at at the top of its 15-32x 12-month range, up from ~15x a year ago, well above the oil industry average of ~18x. Chevron's own historical norms. P/B of 1.91 and P/S of 1.91 are also elevated. with net margin compressed to 5.9% from 7.8% a year ago. ROE at 5.9% from 10.5%. The geopolitical backdrop ( elevated oil prices ($98/bblrel) WTI) a a but is a tail of Hormuz closure) is a tailwind for upstream earnings but creates operational risks (California refining, supply chain disruptions). Management maintained 7-10% production growth guidance and $18-19B capex, with $3-4B structural cost reductions on track. The timing effects are expected to reverse in subsequent quarters, providing a potential earnings tailwind. However, the stock has already rallied ~20% from its Nov 2025 lows, and the current P/E premium prices in much of the upside from elevated oil prices. Near-term catalysts include Q2 earnings (timing effect reversal) and potential Iraq oilfield entry, but these are partially priced in. The score reflects a quality franchise with strong competitive position (Permian, Guyana, integrated model) but at a valuation that leaves limited margin of safety, with near-term earnings volatility creating uncertainty.
